title: tool invoke coalescer: telemetry, fragment signaling, and compatibility adapter
author: Priya Rao
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a compatibility adapter and runtime framing changes to improve OpenAI-style function/tool invocation interoperability, streaming stability, and actionable telemetry. It addresses two classes of failure seen in production canaries: (1) ambiguous tool_choice behavior under tied/confident scoring and (2) stream fragment interleaving that caused downstream tool parsers to misinterpret partial tool messages. The change is deliberately additive and includes fallbacks to preserve compatibility with older agent clients.

Background & motivation: Recent incidents (see SUP-2191) surfaced inconsistent behavior when the model emitted tool selection events concurrently with token-level streaming fragments. Consumers of the OpenAI-compatible envelope sometimes saw truncated tool call payloads or duplicate tool frames. Additionally, we lacked a reliable signal to measure how frequently the model was returning low-confidence tool_choice decisions, limiting our ability to tune routing policies.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add a 'compatibility adapter' layer (src/compat/invoke_adapter.py + schema_mapper) that normalizes historical "function_call" shapes into a single canonical invoke envelope. The adapter handles older schemas, unnamed params, and common shape mismatches.
- Introduce a deterministic tie-breaker for tool_choice semantics and expose a numeric 'tool_choice_confidence' in the canonical envelope. This is used by routing and by telemetry collectors.
- Implement a lightweight streaming fragment signaling protocol (START_TOOL_FRAGMENT / END_TOOL_FRAGMENT markers) at the framer level to avoid downstream reassembly ambiguity. Markers are no-op for clients that don't parse them (backwards compatible).
- Emit three new telemetry counters/histograms: invoke_adapter_latency_ms, tool_choice_confidence (histogram), tool_fragment_repair_count. These are exported to /metrics and surfaced in the Console under the new "Invoke compatibility" dashboard tiles.
- Add unit + integration tests and a controlled canary config to roll the adapter behind a feature flag.

Compatibility and safety: The adapter is installed behind a feature flag. By default, it runs in "observe" mode in canary where it records diffs between native and canonical envelopes without affecting traffic. After canary validation we flip to "enforce" where incoming legacy shapes are normalized. The streaming markers are designed to be ignored by older clients: they are emitted as separate streaming events prefixed with a reserved token so they won't be conflated with JSON payloads.

Testing & rollout plan: Unit tests cover schema mapping permutations; integration tests simulate fragmented streams and concurrent tool selection. Canary config in infra/canary/config.yaml targets 10% traffic for 72h with automated anomaly detection on tool_fragment_repair_count and invoke_adapter_latency_ms.

Related work: builds on ENG-3245 (tool-call stability work) and references earlier adapter efforts ENG-3301.

Changelog (single-line): compatibility adapter + streaming fragment markers + telemetry for tool_choice; canary gated and non-breaking by default.
commits: a1b2c3e: feat(compat): add invoke_adapter + schema mapper with normalization rules
d4e5f6a: perf(stream): implement fragment signaling and framer-level markers
b7c8d9e: telemetry: record tool_choice_confidence and invoke_adapter_latency_ms
c0d1e2f: test: add unit and integration tests for fragmented invokes
f3a4b5c: docs: add openai-compat tool-invoke guide and rollout notes
review_thread: Dylan Berger: Please add an explicit test for tie-breaker determinism when two tools have identical scores — otherwise routing could oscillate. (requested changes)
Priya Rao: Added deterministic tie-breaker test and explanation in schema_mapper docstring. PTAL.
Marcus Li: Can we avoid adding noise to token streams for clients that don't opt-in? How will this interact with our streaming parsers? (question)

Priya Rao: Fragment markers are emitted as reserved prefixed events that parsing clients ignore; added a small adapter in the framer to coalesce markers with payloads when running in legacy compatibility mode.
Elena Novak: Telemetry looks good — add an alert that fires if tool_fragment_repair_count spikes during canary. (approved with comment)
Dylan Berger: LGTM after addressing comments. (approved)
release_notes: Add compatibility adapter for OpenAI-style function/tool calls, deterministic tool_choice semantics, streaming fragment markers to stabilize tool message reassembly, and new telemetry: tool_choice_confidence/invoke_adapter_latency/tool_fragment_repair_count. Canary gated; non-breaking by default.
